Good morning, and welcome to our session today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you've taken this time for yourself, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As we navigate this postpartum journey together, I want to assure you that everything we discuss is confidential and respected.

Today, we'll be using the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and if there's anything we can do to support you better during this time. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource for us to ensure you're receiving the care you need. Please know that this assessment is not about making any diagnoses but rather about creating a safe and supportive space for you to express your feelings and concerns.

We'll go through 10 questions together, and I want you to feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and emotions with me. This is your time, and I'm here to listen without judgment. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll be taking some notes to help me better understand your responses.

Let's get started, shall we? The first question is about how you've been feeling over the past week. Can you tell me a little bit about how you've been feeling, especially in terms of being able to enjoy the things you usually like to do?

Honestly, it's been really tough lately. I just feel so tired all the time, and it's hard to enjoy the things I used to love doing. Even simple things like taking a walk or reading a book, which I used to find so relaxing, just feel like chores now. I mean, I'm happy to see my baby smile and all, but it's just so overwhelming taking care of her. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most days. I've tried to do some of the things I enjoyed before, like painting, but I just can't seem to get into it like I used to. It's like the joy has been sucked out of everything. And to be honest, some days I just feel really sad and discouraged, like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom. It's hard to explain, but it feels like everything is just a bit too much for me to handle right now. (pausing, getting a bit choked up) Sorry, it's just...being a mom is supposed to be this wonderful, happy experience, and I feel like I'm just not feeling that way most of the time.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll catch myself smiling when my baby does something cute, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. I feel like I'm just so worried all the time about everything - is she eating enough, is she sleeping enough, is she healthy...it's just this constant anxiety that's always there, lurking in the back of my mind. And it's hard to laugh and see the funny side of things when you're feeling so overwhelmed and stressed out all the time. I do try to watch funny videos or TV shows to take my mind off things, but even that doesn't seem to be working as well as it used to. It's like my sense of humor has just been dulled or something. (pausing, looking down) I feel like I've lost a part of myself, you know? The part that could just relax and have fun. Now, everything just feels so serious and stressful all the time.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really, no. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like too much effort. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going out with friends or trying a new restaurant, just seem like too much work now. I feel like I'm already so exhausted from taking care of the baby, and the thought of doing something else, even if it's something I used to love, just feels overwhelming. I've had to cancel plans with friends a few times because I just didn't have the energy to get out of the house, and that's been really hard for me. I feel like I'm missing out on things and that I'm just not living the life I want to be living right now. (sighing) And it's not just big things, either - even little things, like looking forward to a cup of coffee in the morning or a warm bath at night, just don't seem to bring me the same joy that they used to. Everything just feels so...flat, I guess. (looking down, fidgeting with hands)
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Oh, yeah...that's definitely been happening a lot lately. I feel like I'm just not doing a good enough job as a mom, and when things go wrong, I immediately start thinking that it's my fault. Like, if the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I figure this out?" Or, if I'm feeling really tired and I need to take a break, I'll think, "You're a terrible mom for not being able to handle this." It's like, I know intellectually that it's okay to make mistakes and that I'm doing the best I can, but emotionally, it's hard for me to shake the feeling that I'm just not good enough. And it's not just with the baby, either - I'll blame myself for things like not having a clean house or not cooking a healthy meal, even though I know those things aren't necessarily important right now. It's just this constant self-doubt and self-criticism that's really hard to deal with. (looking up, tears in eyes) Sometimes I just feel like I'm just not cut out for this whole mom thing, and that's a really scary feeling.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, that's been happening a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something for no reason. Like, I'll think, "What if she stops breathing?" or "What if I'm not producing enough milk?" or "What if I'm not doing everything just right?" And it's not just about the baby, either - I'll worry about things like, "What if my husband loses his job?" or "What if the house catches on fire?" It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that's always there, even when everything is fine. And the worst part is, I know it's irrational. I know that I'm being a good mom and that everything is okay, but I just can't seem to shake the feeling of worry. It's like my mind is just constantly racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and it's exhausting. (taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start feeling this overwhelming sense of anxiety, and I won't even know what I'm anxious about. It's just this general feeling of dread that's always lurking in the back of my mind. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) It's really hard to deal with, and it's making it hard for me to enjoy this time with my baby, which is supposed to be so special.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yes, that's happened to me too. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it or how to make it stop. Sometimes it's triggered by something specific, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just seems to come out of nowhere. (taking a deep breath) I've had a few times where I've been holding the baby and I've just felt this overwhelming sense of panic, like I'm not safe or something. It's a really terrifying feeling, because I know I need to be calm and rational for the baby's sake, but my body just seems to be reacting in this really intense way. (looking up, eyes wide with fear) And the worst part is, I'm scared that something's going to happen to the baby when I'm feeling like that. Like, what if I drop her or something? It's just this constant fear of not being able to protect her, and it's really hard to deal with. (pausing, taking a few deep breaths) Sorry, just talking about it is making me a bit anxious... (fidgeting with hands)
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, looking overwhelmed) Yes, that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly worrying about something - is she eating enough, is she sleeping enough, is she happy? And on top of that, I'm trying to manage the household, and cook meals, and do laundry...it's just too much. (sighing) Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just start feeling like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities. I'll think to myself, "How am I going to get everything done? How am I going to be a good mom and a good wife and a good person?" It's just this constant feeling of being overwhelmed, like I'm in way over my head. (looking down, shaking head) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm not doing anything well. I'm not being a good mom, I'm not being a good wife, I'm not even taking care of myself...it's just this feeling of failure, all the time. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry, it's just...it's really hard to explain, but it feels like everything is just getting on top of me, and I don't know how to get out from under it all.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, looking tired) Yes, that's been a big problem for me. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping through the night, I'll lie awake for hours, just feeling unhappy and overwhelmed. My mind will start racing, and I'll think about all the things that are worrying me, and I just can't seem to calm down. (sighing) And then, when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these really vivid, stressful dreams that leave me feeling anxious and on edge. It's like my brain is just constantly working, even when I'm trying to rest. (rubbing eyes) I'm so tired all the time, but I just can't seem to get the sleep I need. And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem - it's the feeling of being unhappy and unfulfilled that's just always there, lurking in the back of my mind. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Some nights, I'll just lie there and cry, feeling like I'm just so alone and so overwhelmed. It's like I'm drowning in my own emotions, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry, it's just...it's really hard to talk about, but I feel like I'm just so unhappy, and it's affecting every part of my life.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes, that's been me for a while now. I just feel so sad and miserable, like I'm stuck in this dark cloud that I don't know how to escape. Even when good things happen, like the baby smiles at me or my husband does something sweet, I just can't seem to shake off this feeling of sadness. It's like it's just always there, lurking beneath the surface, waiting to pounce. (wiping away tears) I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. It's not just about the baby, either - it's about everything. I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm just a shadow of the person I used to be. I miss my old life, my old self, my old sense of purpose. (sighing) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm supposed to be happy. I'm supposed to be this joyful, loving mother, but instead I just feel like I'm faking it all the time. I'm so scared that someone will find out that I'm not really happy, that I'm just pretending to be this person that I'm not. (looking down, voice cracking) It's just this constant feeling of sadness and misery, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sorry, it's just...it's really hard to talk about, but I feel like I'm just so lost and alone right now.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes, that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just burst into tears. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, or even just walking down the street, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not just a little tear or two, either - it's like a full-on sobbing fit. (wiping away tears with sleeve) I've cried in front of my husband, in front of my family, even in front of strangers. It's like I just can't control it anymore. (sighing) And it's not just about being unhappy, either - it's about feeling overwhelmed, and anxious, and scared. It's like my emotions are just so raw and exposed, and I don't know how to protect myself from them. (sniffling) I've tried to hide it, to put on a brave face and pretend like everything is okay, but it's just not working. I feel like I'm just so vulnerable, like I'm walking around with this huge, gaping wound that's just waiting to be exposed. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And the worst part is, I don't know how to make it stop. I don't know how to make the crying stop, or the sadness stop, or the anxiety stop. I just feel like I'm stuck in this never-ending cycle of emotions, and I don't know how to escape. (sobbing)
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking head) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through this, but I've never thought about harming myself. (pausing, looking relieved) I'm just really glad that's not something I've struggled with. I know that's a really serious thing, and I'm grateful that I haven't had to deal with those kinds of thoughts. (sighing) I just feel like I've been struggling to cope with everything, and I'm trying to find ways to manage my emotions and take care of myself. But harming myself is not something that's ever crossed my mind. (looking up, smiling slightly) I'm just trying to focus on getting through each day, and finding ways to be happy and healthy for my baby and my family.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns, including persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and enjoyment in activities, difficulty coping with responsibilities, anxiety about the baby's well-being, sleep difficulties, feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and self-doubt, anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed, and frequent crying spells and emotional distress. The patient's symptoms and concerns are consistent with potential postpartum depression and anxiety.

They also mention feeling lost and alone, and that the feeling of sadness is always lurking beneath the surface, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates frequent and intense crying, describing it as a 'full-on sobbing fit' that occurs often and in various situations, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and concerns are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's EPDS score of 26 indicates a high level of emotional distress and risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. The patient's reports of <quote>feeling sad and miserable</quote>, <quote>difficulty coping with responsibilities</quote>, and <quote>frequent crying spells</quote> are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria</med> for <med>Major Depressive Disorder</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices
3. Recommend stress management techniques, such as deep breathing and meditation
4. Support patient in seeking social support from family and friends
5. Consider referral to <med>mental health specialist</med> for further evaluation and treatment
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
